proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(c\in\mathcal C\), \(1\le\ell\le d_c\), and \(1\le f\le L\). Write \(t=t_{c\ell}\), \(Q=Q_c\), \(G=G_c\), \(\bar Q=\widehat Q_{c,-f}\), and \(\bar G=\widehat G_{c,-f}\), and condition on the sigma-field \(\mathcal T_{cf}\) generated by the observations used to train \(\bar Q\) and \(\bar G\). The validation observations are independent of \(\mathcal T_{cf}\) and have law \(P_c\) by Assumption~\ref{ass:cell-iid}. The inverse-survival metric in Assumption~\ref{ass:censor-estimability} makes \(1/\bar G\) finite on the required horizon with probability tending to one. All quotient formulas use the convention in Definition~\ref{def:aipcw-score}.

For one validation observation define
\[
 N(u)=\mathbf 1\{U\le u,\Delta=1\},
 \qquad
 Y(u)=\mathbf 1\{U\ge u\}.
\]
Assumption~\ref{ass:conditional-censoring}, the tie convention \(\Delta=\mathbf 1\{T\le C\}\), and the left-continuous definition \(G(u\mid X)=P(C\ge u\mid X)\) imply
\[
 E\{dN(u)\mid X\}=Q(u-\mid X)G(u\mid X)\Lambda(du\mid X),
 \qquad
 E\{Y(u)\mid X\}=Q(u-\mid X)G(u\mid X).
\]
Assumption~\ref{ass:event-origin-support} excludes an event atom at zero. Taking the conditional expectation in Definition~\ref{def:aipcw-score} and interchanging expectation with each finite nonnegative hazard integral gives
\[
 E\{\psi_t(O;\bar Q,\bar G)\mid X,\mathcal T_{cf}\}
 =\bar Q(t\mid X)\left[1+\int_{(0,t]}
 \frac{Q(u-\mid X)G(u\mid X)}{\bar Q(u\mid X)\bar G(u\mid X)}
 (\bar\Lambda-\Lambda)(du\mid X)\right].
\]
Here and below an integral against \(\bar\Lambda-\Lambda\) is the difference of the two finite Stieltjes integrals.

Put \(R(u\mid X)=Q(u\mid X)/\bar Q(u\mid X)-1\). The product-integral quotient rule gives
\[
 dR(u\mid X)=\frac{Q(u-\mid X)}{\bar Q(u\mid X)}
 (\bar\Lambda-\Lambda)(du\mid X).
\]
Indeed, at a jump time, the identities
\(Q(u)=Q(u-)\{1-\Delta\Lambda(u)\}\) and
\(\bar Q(u)=\bar Q(u-)\{1-\Delta\bar\Lambda(u)\}\) give
\[
 \Delta(Q/\bar Q)(u)=\frac{Q(u-)}{\bar Q(u)}
 \{\Delta\bar\Lambda(u)-\Delta\Lambda(u)\},
\]
and the continuous part is the ordinary quotient rule. Assumptions~\ref{ass:event-origin-support} and~\ref{ass:learner-origin-normalization} give \(R(0\mid X)=0\), so integration yields
\[
 Q(t\mid X)=\bar Q(t\mid X)\left[1+\int_{(0,t]}
 \frac{Q(u-\mid X)}{\bar Q(u\mid X)}
 (\bar\Lambda-\Lambda)(du\mid X)\right].
\]
Subtracting this identity from the conditional score mean proves the exact remainder
\[
 \mathfrak R_{cf\ell}(X)
 :=E\{\psi_t(O;\bar Q,\bar G)\mid X,\mathcal T_{cf}\}-Q(t\mid X)
 =\bar Q(t\mid X)\int_{(0,t]}
 \left\{\frac{G(u\mid X)}{\bar G(u\mid X)}-1\right\}
 dR(u\mid X).
\]
It vanishes when either fitted nuisance is its truth, so no first-order event- or censor-nuisance term remains.

Let
\[
 A_{cf\ell}(X)=\sup_{0\le u\le t}
 \left|\frac1{\bar G(u\mid X)}-\frac1{G(u\mid X)}\right|.
\]
Since \(0\le\bar Q(t\mid X)\le1\), \(0\le G(u\mid X)\le1\), and Assumption~\ref{ass:relative-survival-bv} makes \(dR\) a finite signed measure, the preceding identity and the definition of \(V_{cf\ell}\) imply
\[
 |\mathfrak R_{cf\ell}(X)|\le A_{cf\ell}(X)V_{cf\ell}(X).
\]
Assumption~\ref{ass:censor-estimability} gives \(\|A_{cf\ell}\|_{L_2(P_c)}=O_P(b_K)\), while Assumption~\ref{ass:relative-survival-variation-rate} gives \(\|V_{cf\ell}\|_{L_2(P_c)}=O_P(a_K)\). Conditional Cauchy--Schwarz and Assumption~\ref{ass:nuisance-product-rate} therefore give, jointly over the fixed indices,
\[
 \left|P_c\{\psi_t(\bar Q,\bar G)-\psi_t(Q,G)\}\right|
 \le\|A_{cf\ell}\|_{L_2(P_c)}\|V_{cf\ell}\|_{L_2(P_c)}
 =O_P(a_Kb_K)=o_P(K^{-1/2}).
\]
This use of the relative-variation rate is explicit and conditional on the selected learner; it is not derived from generic nuisance consistency.

We next control the cross-fitted empirical term and the fitted influence function. Define
\[
 r_t(u\mid X)=\frac{Q(t\mid X)}{Q(u\mid X)},
 \qquad
 \bar r_t(u\mid X)=\frac{\bar Q(t\mid X)}{\bar Q(u\mid X)},
 \qquad 0\le u\le t.
\]
Both are nondecreasing in \(u\), take values in \([0,1]\), and satisfy
\(d\bar r_t(u\mid X)=\bar r_t(u\mid X)\bar\Lambda(du\mid X)\). With \(w=t\wedge U\), the score can therefore be written
\[
 \psi_t(O;\bar Q,\bar G)
 =\bar Q(t\mid X)
 -\mathbf 1\{U\le t,\Delta=1\}\frac{\bar r_t(U\mid X)}{\bar G(U\mid X)}
 +\int_{(0,w]}\frac1{\bar G(u\mid X)}\,d\bar r_t(u\mid X).
\]
Set
\[
 D_{Q,cf\ell}(X)=\sup_{0\le u\le t}
 |\bar r_t(u\mid X)-r_t(u\mid X)|.
\]
Assumption~\ref{ass:event-estimability} gives \(\|D_{Q,cf\ell}\|_{L_2(P_c)}=O_P(a_K)\). Assumption~\ref{ass:censor-positivity} gives \(1/G\le g^{-1}\); since \(G\) is nonincreasing, \(1/G\) is nondecreasing and has variation at most \(g^{-1}-1\) on the horizon. Split the integral difference as
\[
 \int_{(0,w]}\left(\frac1{\bar G}-\frac1G\right)d\bar r_t
 +\int_{(0,w]}\frac1G\,d(\bar r_t-r_t).
\]
The first term is bounded by \(A_{cf\ell}(X)\), because \(\bar r_t\) has variation at most one. Stieltjes integration by parts bounds the second by its two endpoint terms plus
\(D_{Q,cf\ell}(X)\operatorname{TV}(1/G)\). The baseline and event terms in the score difference satisfy the same type of bound. Thus, for a finite constant \(C_g\),
\[
 \|\psi_t(\bar Q,\bar G)-\psi_t(Q,G)\|_{L_2(P_c)}
 \le C_g\{\|D_{Q,cf\ell}\|_{L_2(P_c)}+\|A_{cf\ell}\|_{L_2(P_c)}\}
 =O_P(a_K+b_K)=o_P(1),
\]
where the last equality uses Assumptions~\ref{ass:event-rate-vanishes} and~\ref{ass:censor-rate-vanishes}.

Let \(n_{cf}=|\mathcal V_{cf}|\), let \(\mathbb P_{cf}\) be the validation empirical measure for a nonempty fold, and set \(\widehat\psi_{cf\ell}=\psi_t(\mathord\cdot;\bar Q,\bar G)\) and \(\psi_{c\ell}=\psi_t(\mathord\cdot;Q,G)\). Empty folds contribute zero. Setting \((\bar Q,\bar G)=(Q,G)\) in the exact mean identity shows \(P_c\psi_{c\ell}=S_c(t)\). Since the folds partition \(\{1,ldots,K\}\), Definition~\ref{def:cell-estimator} gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widehat s_{c\ell}-S_c(t)
 &=K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\phi_{c\ell}(O_{ci})\\
 &\quad+\sum_{f=1}^L\frac{n_{cf}}K
 (\mathbb P_{cf}-P_c)(\widehat\psi_{cf\ell}-\psi_{c\ell})\\
 &\quad+\sum_{f=1}^L\frac{n_{cf}}K
 P_c(\widehat\psi_{cf\ell}-\psi_{c\ell}).
\end{aligned}
\]
Conditional on \(\mathcal T_{cf}\), the standard deviation of the \(f\)-th weighted empirical term is at most
\[
 \frac{\sqrt{n_{cf}}}{K}
 \|\widehat\psi_{cf\ell}-\psi_{c\ell}\|_{L_2(P_c)}
 \le K^{-1/2}o_P(1).
\]
Conditional Chebyshev and fixed \(L\) make their sum \(o_P(K^{-1/2})\). The bias sum is \(O_P(a_Kb_K)=o_P(K^{-1/2})\), because its weights sum to one. Consequently
\[
 \sqrt K\{\widehat s_{c\ell}-S_c(t)\}
 =K^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^K\phi_{c\ell}(O_{ci})+o_P(1).
\]

Assumption~\ref{ass:fixed-panel} makes the numbers of cells, folds, and coordinates fixed, so a finite union bound makes the expansion joint. Assumption~\ref{ass:cross-cell-independence} permits stacking the cell influences with a common within-cell index \(i\), giving the asserted expansion for \((\widehat y,\widehat M,\widehat B,\widehat s_1)\) with influence \(\Phi_i\).

For an observation in fold \(f\), define
\[
 \widehat\phi_{c\ell,i}=\widehat\psi_{cf\ell}(O_{ci})-\widehat s_{c\ell}.
\]
The expansion gives \(|\widehat s_{c\ell}-S_c(t)|=o_P(1)\), and the fitted-score bound gives
\[
 \|\widehat\phi_{c\ell}-\phi_{c\ell}\|_{L_2(P_c)}
 \le\|\widehat\psi_{cf\ell}-\psi_{c\ell}\|_{L_2(P_c)}
 +|\widehat s_{c\ell}-S_c(t)|=o_P(1).
\]
Assumption~\ref{ass:influence-moment} ensures the required second moments. A finite union bound proves joint foldwise \(L_2(P_c)\)-consistency of the plug-in influence vectors and completes the proof.

Let \(Z=(y,M,B,s_1)\), with matrix blocks vectorized in a fixed order, and let \(\widehat Z=(\widehat y,\widehat M,\widehat B,\widehat s_1)\). Assumption~\ref{ass:fixed-panel} makes its dimension fixed. Lemma~\ref{lem:joint-cell-expansion}, which is conditional on the disclosed bounded-variation and relative-variation learner restrictions, gives
\[
 \widehat Z-Z=K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_i+r_K,
 \qquad \sqrt K\|r_K\|_2\to_P0.
\]
Each \(\Phi_i\) is centered by the definition of \(\phi_c\). Assumptions~\ref{ass:cell-iid} and~\ref{ass:cross-cell-independence} make \(\Phi_1,\ldots,\Phi_K\) independent and identically distributed as vectors, and Assumptions~\ref{ass:influence-moment} and~\ref{ass:fixed-panel} give
\[
 E\Phi_i=0,
 \qquad E\|\Phi_i\|_2^{2+\nu}<\infty.
\]
Consequently \(E\|K^{-1/2}\sum_i\Phi_i\|_2^2=E\|\Phi_i\|_2^2<\infty\), and Markov's inequality yields
\[
 \|\widehat Z-Z\|_2=O_P(K^{-1/2}),
 \qquad \|\widehat M-M\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_P(K^{-1/2}).
\]

Assumptions~\ref{ass:exact-rank} and~\ref{ass:singular-gap} give \(M_r=M\), \(P=M^+\), and \(\|P\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\kappa^{-1}\). Lemma~\ref{lem:full-spectral-differential} makes \(\mathcal F(y,M,B)=yM_r^+B\) Fr\'echet differentiable on a neighborhood of the truth. Since \(\widehat Z\to_PZ\), its first-order expansion, Definition~\ref{def:full-spectral-map}, and the preceding root-\(K\) rate give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widehat\theta-\theta
 &=(\widehat y-y)PB+y\mathcal L_M(\widehat M-M)B+yP(\widehat B-B)+o_P(K^{-1/2})\\
 &=K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K
 \{\Phi_{y,i}PB+y\mathcal L_M(\Phi_{M,i})B+yP\Phi_{B,i}\}
 +o_P(K^{-1/2})\\
 &=K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_{\theta,i}+o_P(K^{-1/2}).
\end{aligned}
\]
The factual-post block of Lemma~\ref{lem:joint-cell-expansion} is
\[
 \widehat s_1-s_1=K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_{1,i}+o_P(K^{-1/2}).
\]
Stacking and applying Definition~\ref{def:transported-influence} proves the stated asymptotic linear representation. In particular, it retains perturbations of the target-pre, donor-pre, and donor-post learned blocks.

Definition~\ref{def:transported-influence} is a fixed linear transformation of \(\Phi_i\). Its coefficients are finite because \(P\) is bounded and the explicit formula in Definition~\ref{def:full-differential} makes \(\mathcal L_M\) bounded. Hence
\[
 E\Phi_{\eta,i}=0,
 \qquad E\|\Phi_{\eta,i}\|_2^{2+\nu}<\infty,
 \qquad E(\Phi_{\eta,i}\Phi_{\eta,i}^\top)=\Omega_\eta.
\]
To derive the possibly singular Gaussian limit directly, fix \(a\in\mathbb R^{2J}\), put \(W_i=a^\top\Phi_{\eta,i}\), \(\omega_a^2=a^\top\Omega_\eta a\), and \(\delta=\min(\nu,1)>0\). Taylor's formula on \(|x|\le1\), combined with the boundedness of \(e^{\mathrm i x}\) on \(|x|>1\), gives a finite \(C_\delta\) such that
\[
 \left|e^{\mathrm i x}-1-\mathrm i x+\frac{x^2}{2}\right|
 \le C_\delta|x|^{2+\delta}.
\]
Therefore
\[
 \left|Ee^{\mathrm iW_i/\sqrt K}-1+\frac{\omega_a^2}{2K}\right|
 \le C_\delta K^{-1-\delta/2}E|W_i|^{2+\delta}=o(K^{-1}).
\]
Independence gives
\[
 E\exp\!\left\{\mathrm i a^\top K^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_{\eta,i}\right\}
 \longrightarrow\exp(-\omega_a^2/2).
\]
This is the characteristic function of \(\mathcal N_{2J}(0,\Omega_\eta)\), including when \(\Omega_\eta\) is singular. The continuity criterion for characteristic functions and the asymptotic linear representation prove the joint limit without a full-covariance lower bound.

For plug-in consistency, let \(\Pi_R(A)\) be the projector onto the leading \(r\) right singular vectors of a matrix \(A\) near \(M\). The variational characterization of singular values gives
\[
 |\sigma_j(A)-\sigma_j(M)|\le\|A-M\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]
Exact rank and the gap \(\sigma_r(M)\ge\kappa\) make the leading projector unique locally. If \(A_m\to M\), compactness of the rank-\(r\) projector set and uniqueness of the maximizer of \(Q\mapsto\operatorname{tr}(QA^\top A)\) show \(\Pi_R(A_m)\to\Pi_R(M)\). Thus \(A_r=A\Pi_R(A)\to M\), and
\[
 A_r^+=\{A_r^\top A_r+I-\Pi_R(A)\}^{-1}A_r^\top.
\]
The matrix in braces has eigenvalues \(\sigma_1(A)^2,\ldots,\sigma_r(A)^2,1,\ldots,1\), bounded away from zero locally. Continuity of inversion and substitution into Definition~\ref{def:full-differential} therefore give
\[
 (\widehat M)_r^+\to_PP,
 \qquad \widehat{\mathcal L}_{\widehat M}\to_P\mathcal L_M
\]
in the relevant operator norms.

Let \(\widehat\Phi_i\) stack the fold-specific fitted cell influences. Lemma~\ref{lem:joint-cell-expansion} and conditional Markov inequalities over the fixed cells and folds give
\[
 K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\|\widehat\Phi_i-\Phi_i\|_2^2=o_P(1).
\]
Let \(\mathsf A\) be the fixed linear transport in Definition~\ref{def:transported-influence} and \(\widehat{\mathsf A}\) its plug-in version. Consistency of the input blocks and the preceding spectral convergences imply
\[
 \|\widehat{\mathsf A}-\mathsf A\|_{\mathrm{op}}=o_P(1),
 \qquad \|\widehat{\mathsf A}\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_P(1).
\]
The weak law gives \(K^{-1}\sum_i\|\Phi_i\|_2^2=O_P(1)\). Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
 K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\|\widehat\Phi_{\eta,i}-\Phi_{\eta,i}\|_2^2
 &\le2\|\widehat{\mathsf A}\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2K^{-1}\sum_i\|\widehat\Phi_i-\Phi_i\|_2^2\\
 &\quad+2\|\widehat{\mathsf A}-\mathsf A\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2K^{-1}\sum_i\|\Phi_i\|_2^2=o_P(1).
\end{aligned}
\]

Write \(D_i=\widehat\Phi_{\eta,i}-\Phi_{\eta,i}\). Expanding outer products and applying Cauchy--Schwarz yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\left\|\widehat\Omega_\eta-K^{-1}\sum_i\Phi_{\eta,i}\Phi_{\eta,i}^\top\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\\
 &\quad\le
 \left(K^{-1}\sum_i\|D_i\|_2^2\right)^{1/2}
 \left\{\left(K^{-1}\sum_i\|\widehat\Phi_{\eta,i}\|_2^2\right)^{1/2}
 +\left(K^{-1}\sum_i\|\Phi_{\eta,i}\|_2^2\right)^{1/2}\right\}=o_P(1).
\end{aligned}
\]
Every coordinate product of \(\Phi_{\eta,i}\) is integrable by Cauchy--Schwarz, so the scalar weak law applied entrywise, with fixed \(2J\), gives
\[
 K^{-1}\sum_i\Phi_{\eta,i}\Phi_{\eta,i}^\top\to_P\Omega_\eta.
\]
This proves \(\widehat\Omega_\eta\to_P\Omega_\eta\), again without requiring positive definiteness.

Finally, Lemma~\ref{lem:joint-cell-expansion} centers every cell estimator at the observed-law functional \(S_c(t)=E\{Q_c(t\mid X_{ci})\}\), rather than a marginal Kaplan--Meier pseudo-target. Assumption~\ref{ass:post-transport}, by itself, equates the target unit's untreated post-treatment survival row with \(yM_r^+B\); no row-space premise on \(y\) is used for this theorem. The factual row \(s_1\) remains the treated post-period survival curve. Thus post-transport is the causal-identification equality connecting the observed-law spectral functional to the untreated causal curve, and the proof is complete.

Let \(\Omega_\theta\) and \(\widehat\Omega_\theta\) denote the counterfactual \(J\times J\) principal blocks of \(\Omega_\eta\) and \(\widehat\Omega_\eta\). Theorem~\ref{thm:joint-spectral-limit} gives \(\widehat\Omega_\theta\to_P\Omega_\theta\), even when these matrices are singular. Put \(\sigma_j^2=(\Omega_\theta)_{jj}=\operatorname{Var}(\Phi_{\theta,i,j})\). Assumption~\ref{ass:counterfactual-coordinate-variance} gives
\[
 \min_{1\le j\le J}\sigma_j^2\ge v>0,
 \qquad \widehat\sigma_j\to_P\sigma_j>0.
\]
Thus every division in Definition~\ref{def:multiplier-band} is well defined with probability tending to one; any convention on the complementary event is asymptotically irrelevant.

Conditionally on the sample,
\[
 Z_K^*=K^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^K\xi_i\widehat\Phi_{\theta,i}
\]
is exactly centered Gaussian with covariance \(\widehat\Omega_\theta\). Its studentized covariance is
\[
 \widehat R_K
 =\operatorname{diag}(\widehat\Omega_\theta)^{-1/2}
 \widehat\Omega_\theta
 \operatorname{diag}(\widehat\Omega_\theta)^{-1/2}
 \to_P
 R=\operatorname{diag}(\Omega_\theta)^{-1/2}
 \Omega_\theta
 \operatorname{diag}(\Omega_\theta)^{-1/2}.
\]
Both \(R\) and \(\widehat R_K\) are positive semidefinite and \(R_{jj}=1\); positive definiteness is not asserted.

Let \(Z\sim\mathcal N_J(0,R)\) and \(H=\max_j|Z_j|\). Each marginal \(Z_j\) is standard normal. For every \(t\ge0\),
\[
 \{H=t\}\subseteq\bigcup_{j=1}^J\{|Z_j|=t\},
\]
and every event on the right has probability zero. Hence \(H\) is atomless. It is also strictly increasing on its range. Indeed, let \(S=\operatorname{range}(R)\), the support subspace of \(Z\). For \(0\le x_1<x_2\), choose a nonzero \(z_0\in S\) and scale it so that \(x_1<\|z_0\|_\infty<x_2\). The shell
\[
 \{z\in S:x_1<\|z\|_\infty<x_2\}
\]
is then a nonempty relatively open subset of \(S\). The restriction of the Gaussian law to \(S\) has a strictly positive density with respect to Lebesgue measure on \(S\), because \(R\) is positive definite on its range. The shell consequently has positive probability. Thus the distribution function of \(H\) is continuous and strictly increasing, and its \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile \(c_{1-\alpha}\) is unique.

The positive-semidefinite square-root map is continuous in fixed dimension. If \(\varepsilon\sim\mathcal N_J(0,I_J)\), then along every subsequence on which \(\widehat R_K\to R\), a further subsequence converges almost surely and
\[
 \widehat R_K^{1/2}\varepsilon\longrightarrow R^{1/2}\varepsilon
\]
almost surely on the product space. The atomlessness just proved gives convergence of the corresponding conditional distribution functions at every point. Strict increase at the target quantile then gives
\[
 c_{1-\alpha}^\star\to_Pc_{1-\alpha},
 \qquad P(H\le c_{1-\alpha})=1-\alpha.
\]
This subsequence argument establishes convergence in probability for the original sequence.

On the sampling side, Theorem~\ref{thm:joint-spectral-limit}, covariance consistency, and the continuous-mapping theorem yield
\[
 \max_{1\le j\le J}
 \left|\frac{\sqrt K(\widehat\theta_j-\theta_j)}{\widehat\sigma_j}\right|
 \rightsquigarrow H.
\]
Combining this limit, critical-value consistency, and continuity of the law of \(H\) proves
\[
 \Pr\!\left\{\theta_j\in
 \left[\widehat\theta_j\pm c_{1-\alpha}^\star\widehat\sigma_j/\sqrt K\right]
 \text{ for every }1\le j\le J\right\}\to1-\alpha.
\]
Assumption~\ref{ass:fixed-panel} is used to keep \(J\) fixed.

For the scalar grid target, Definition~\ref{def:full-spectral-map}, the definition \(\tau_R=q^\top(s_1-\theta)\), and Theorem~\ref{thm:joint-spectral-limit} imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sqrt K(\widehat\tau_R-\tau_R)
 &=q^\top\sqrt K\{(\widehat s_1-s_1)-(\widehat\theta-\theta)\}\\
 &=K^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^Kq^\top(\Phi_{1,i}-\Phi_{\theta,i})+o_P(1)\\
 &=K^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_{\tau,i}+o_P(1).
\end{aligned}
\]
Assumption~\ref{ass:grid-rmst-variance} gives directly
\[
 V_R=\operatorname{Var}\{q^\top(\Phi_{1,i}-\Phi_{\theta,i})\}\ge v>0.
\]
No lower bound on any other direction of \(\Omega_\eta\) is used. The empirical \(L_2\)-consistency in Theorem~\ref{thm:joint-spectral-limit} and Cauchy--Schwarz imply
\[
 \left|\widehat V_R-K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_{\tau,i}^2\right|=o_P(1).
\]
Since \(E\Phi_{\tau,i}^2<\infty\), the weak law gives \(K^{-1}\sum_i\Phi_{\tau,i}^2\to_PV_R\). Hence \(\widehat V_R\to_PV_R>0\). The scalar projection of the joint Gaussian limit and Slutsky's theorem give
\[
 \frac{\sqrt K(\widehat\tau_R-\tau_R)}{\sqrt{\widehat V_R}}
 \rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1).
\]
Therefore
\[
 \left[\widehat\tau_R-z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat V_R/K},
 \widehat\tau_R+z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat V_R/K}\right]
\]
has limiting coverage \(1-\alpha\). This conclusion concerns the declared fixed-grid functional and not a continuous-time RMST integral.

added_lemmas.statement:
Suppose that, in every cell, the supports of \(X_{ci}\) and of event times through the fixed horizon \(\max_\ell t_{c\ell}\) are finite and do not depend on \(K\). Suppose there are fixed positive constants such that, uniformly over cells, covariate strata, and event-support times on the horizon, the probability \(P_c\{X_{ci}=x,U_{ci}\ge u\}\) is bounded below, the conditional event hazard
\[
 h_c(u\mid x)=P_c(T_{ci}=u\mid T_{ci}\ge u,X_{ci}=x)
\]
is bounded away from one, and every training complement of \(\mathcal V_{cf}\) has at least a fixed positive multiple of \(K\) observations. On that training sample, let \(N_{cfxu}\) count \(\{X_{ci}=x,U_{ci}=u,\Delta_{ci}=1\}\), let \(Y_{cfxu}\) count \(\{X_{ci}=x,U_{ci}\ge u\}\), estimate \(h_c(u\mid x)\) by the ratio \(N_{cfxu}/(Y_{cfxu}\vee1)\) clipped to an interval \([0,1-\varepsilon/2]\) containing every true hazard, and form \(\widehat Q_{c,-f}\) by the finite product integral of these hazards, normalized to one at time zero. Then, uniformly over the fixed cells, folds, strata, and times,
\[
 \left|\widehat h_{c,-f}(u\mid x)-h_c(u\mid x)\right|=O_P(K^{-1/2}),
 \qquad
 \operatorname{TV}\!\left[\log\!\left\{Q_c/\widehat Q_{c,-f}\right\}\right]=O_P(K^{-1/2}),
\]
the event-survival ratio error is \(O_P(K^{-1/2})\), the path \(R_{cf}\) is of bounded variation, and
\[
 \max_{c,f,\ell}\left\|V_{cf\ell}(X_{ci})\right\|_{L_2(P_c)}=O_P(K^{-1/2}).
\]
Thus this finite-stratum learner satisfies the event-side conditions with \(a_K=K^{-1/2}\). Every censor-survival learner satisfying Assumption~\ref{ass:censor-estimability} with \(b_K=o(1)\) then satisfies \(a_Kb_K=o(K^{-1/2})\). This is an attainability certificate for the stated finite-stratum submodel, not a claim about generic learners or the TCL application.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix a cell \(c\), a fold \(f\), a covariate support point \(x\), and an event-support time \(u\) on the required horizon. Write \(I_{cf}=\{1,\ldots,K\}\setminus\mathcal V_{cf}\) and \(n_{cf}=|I_{cf}|\). By hypothesis, \(n_{cf}\ge \rho K\) for a fixed \(\rho>0\). Define the training-sample proportions
\[
 \widehat A_{cfxu}=\frac1{n_{cf}}\sum_{i\in I_{cf}}
 \mathbf 1\{X_{ci}=x,U_{ci}=u,\Delta_{ci}=1\},
 \qquad
 \widehat D_{cfxu}=\frac1{n_{cf}}\sum_{i\in I_{cf}}
 \mathbf 1\{X_{ci}=x,U_{ci}\ge u\}.
\]
Assumption~\ref{ass:cell-iid} makes both averages means of independent Bernoulli variables. Hence their variances are at most \((4n_{cf})^{-1}\le(4\rho K)^{-1}\). Chebyshev's inequality gives
\[
 \widehat A_{cfxu}-A_{cxu}=O_P(K^{-1/2}),
 \qquad
 \widehat D_{cfxu}-D_{cxu}=O_P(K^{-1/2}),
\]
where \(A_{cxu}=P_c(X_{ci}=x,U_{ci}=u,\Delta_{ci}=1)\) and \(D_{cxu}=P_c(X_{ci}=x,U_{ci}\ge u)\). The number of cells, folds, strata, and event-support times is fixed by the proposition and Assumption~\ref{ass:fixed-panel}; a finite union bound makes both rates uniform over all these indices.

The tie convention \(\Delta_{ci}=\mathbf 1\{T_{ci}\le C_{ci}\}\) implies
\[
 \{U_{ci}=u,\Delta_{ci}=1\}=\{T_{ci}=u,C_{ci}\ge u\},
 \qquad
 \{U_{ci}\ge u\}=\{T_{ci}\ge u,C_{ci}\ge u\}.
\]
Assumption~\ref{ass:conditional-censoring} therefore gives, whenever \(P_c(X_{ci}=x)>0\),
\[
 \frac{A_{cxu}}{D_{cxu}}
 =\frac{P_c(T_{ci}=u\mid X_{ci}=x)P_c(C_{ci}\ge u\mid X_{ci}=x)}
 {P_c(T_{ci}\ge u\mid X_{ci}=x)P_c(C_{ci}\ge u\mid X_{ci}=x)}
 =h_c(u\mid x).
\]
The assumed at-risk lower bound gives \(D_{cxu}\ge d_0>0\). On an event whose probability tends to one uniformly, \(\widehat D_{cfxu}\ge d_0/2\), so elementary ratio algebra yields
\[
 \left|\frac{\widehat A_{cfxu}}{\widehat D_{cfxu}}-\frac{A_{cxu}}{D_{cxu}}\right|
 \le \frac{2}{d_0}|\widehat A_{cfxu}-A_{cxu}|
 +\frac{2A_{cxu}}{d_0^2}|\widehat D_{cfxu}-D_{cxu}|
 =O_P(K^{-1/2}).
\]
Replacing a zero empirical denominator by one affects only the complement of this event. Projection onto a closed interval is one-Lipschitz. Because \(h_c(u\mid x)\le1-\varepsilon\) lies in \([0,1-\varepsilon/2]\), clipping preserves the rate and proves
\[
 \max_{c,f,x,u}|\widehat h_{c,-f}(u\mid x)-h_c(u\mid x)|=O_P(K^{-1/2}).
\]

List the at most \(m_0<\infty\) event-support points on a cell horizon in increasing order. Assumption~\ref{ass:event-origin-support} and the finite product-integral construction give
\[
 Q_c(t\mid x)=\prod_{u\le t}\{1-h_c(u\mid x)\},
 \qquad
 \widehat Q_{c,-f}(t\mid x)=\prod_{u\le t}\{1-\widehat h_{c,-f}(u\mid x)\}.
\]
Both products equal one at zero. The derivative of \(z\mapsto\log(1-z)\) has absolute value at most \(2/\varepsilon\) on \([0,1-\varepsilon/2]\). Therefore, for the step path
\(L_{cf}(t\mid x)=\log\{Q_c(t\mid x)/\widehat Q_{c,-f}(t\mid x)\}\),
\[
 \operatorname{TV}\{L_{cf}(\mathord\cdot\mid x);[0,\max_\ell t_{c\ell}]\}
 \le \frac{2}{\varepsilon}\sum_u
 |\widehat h_{c,-f}(u\mid x)-h_c(u\mid x)|
 =O_P(K^{-1/2})
\]
uniformly over \(c,f,x\). In particular, \(\sup_t|L_{cf}(t\mid x)|=O_P(K^{-1/2})\). Since \(R_{cf}=\exp(L_{cf})-1\), composition with the exponential function gives, on the event \(\sup_t|L_{cf}(t\mid x)|\le1\),
\[
 \operatorname{TV}\{R_{cf}(\mathord\cdot\mid x)\}
 \le e\,\operatorname{TV}\{L_{cf}(\mathord\cdot\mid x)\}
 =O_P(K^{-1/2}).
\]
The event has probability tending to one uniformly. This proves bounded variation and its rate.

The hazard separation and finiteness of the support also give the deterministic lower bounds
\[
 \inf_{c,x,t}Q_c(t\mid x)\ge\varepsilon^{m_0}>0,
 \qquad
 \inf_{c,f,x,t}\widehat Q_{c,-f}(t\mid x)\ge(\varepsilon/2)^{m_0}>0.
\]
Finite products and division on this compact positive set are Lipschitz functions of the finite hazard vector. Thus, uniformly for the survival ratios in the event-learner metric,
\[
 \sup_{0\le u\le t\le\max_\ell t_{c\ell}}
 \left|\frac{\widehat Q_{c,-f}(t\mid x)}{\widehat Q_{c,-f}(u\mid x)}
 -\frac{Q_c(t\mid x)}{Q_c(u\mid x)}\right|=O_P(K^{-1/2}).
\]
Because each covariate support is finite,
\[
 \|V_{cf\ell}(X_{ci})\|_{L_2(P_c)}
 \le\max_x\operatorname{TV}\{R_{cf}(\mathord\cdot\mid x);[0,t_{c\ell}]\}
 =O_P(K^{-1/2}),
\]
jointly over the fixed indices. Hence the learner meets the event-ratio and relative-variation conditions with \(a_K=K^{-1/2}\). If a censor learner satisfies Assumption~\ref{ass:censor-estimability} with \(b_K=o(1)\), then
\[
 a_Kb_K=K^{-1/2}b_K=o(K^{-1/2}).
\]
No assertion in this proof extends the finite-support calculation to an arbitrary event learner or verifies its premises for the TCL data.

open_obligations.partial_result:
In a fixed-dimensional orthogonal cell-score experiment, let \(\rho_K\) be a consistently estimable operator-noise scale with \(\|\widehat M-M_K\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_P(\rho_K)\). If larger nonzero singular values stay uniformly separated, the cell expansion and influence estimation hold uniformly over the triangular collection, and standardized moments and the relevant variances are uniformly controlled, then ordinary shrinking-rank spectral inference is uniformly regular on the unrestricted signal-to-noise region
\[
 \Delta_K/\rho_K\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
For any \(h_K\to\infty\) satisfying \(h_K\rho_K/\Delta_K\to0\), thresholding at \(h_K\widehat\rho_K\) selects rank \(r\) uniformly with probability tending to one. On \(\|\widehat M-M_K\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\Delta_K/2\), the standardized second-order spectral remainder is \(O_P(\rho_K/\Delta_K)=o_P(1)\), so the differentiated plug-in and multiplier construction is uniformly honest. Its \(j\)-th half-width has order \(\sigma_{Kj}/\sqrt K\), and it shrinks when \(\max_j\sigma_{Kj}/\sqrt K\to0\).

For \(P_{\lambda,K}=(M_K^\top M_K+\lambda_K^2I)^{-1}M_K^\top\) and \(M_K=\sum_{k=1}^r\sigma_{k,K}u_{k,K}v_{k,K}^\top\), the exact bias relative to the unregularized target is
\[
 yP_{\lambda,K}B-y(M_K)_r^+B
 =-\sum_{k=1}^r\frac{\lambda_K^2}{\sigma_{k,K}^2+\lambda_K^2}
 \frac{yv_{k,K}}{\sigma_{k,K}}u_{k,K}^\top B.
\]
Thus regularization requires explicit bias coverage or a loading restriction. The gap alone is not a complete frontier: if the weak component \((yv_{r,K}/\sigma_{r,K})u_{r,K}^\top B\) vanishes identically on a known subclass, the target equals its rank-\((r-1)\) version and remains regular even at a closed gap. Conversely, on an unrestricted class allowing an active weak component and local perturbations in that singular direction, mutually contiguous paths with \(\Delta_K\asymp\rho_K\) can have a fixed separation in \(y(M_K)_r^+B\). Therefore no uniformly consistent estimator, and no uniformly honest band with shrinking diameter for \(0<\alpha<1/2\), exists on that remaining class. Promoting this conditional characterization to the frozen question requires a declared uniform triangular AIPCW experiment, operator-noise calibration, uniform moment and variance bounds, and a loading class; these are not supplied by the fixed-law cell lemma or by the finite-stratum attainability certificate.

prose_updates.tldr: For fixed donor count, pre grid, post grid, rank, and a separated nonzero singular spectrum, covariate-adjusted cross-fitted AIPCW cell estimates have a joint root-\(K\) expansion conditional on explicit bounded-variation and relative-variation restrictions for the selected event learner. A clipped empirical hazard learner satisfies those restrictions with \(a_K=K^{-1/2}\) on a fixed finite-stratum submodel, but this certificate is not a generic learner result and does not verify the TCL application. Exact post-transport, without a target-pre row-space premise, identifies the untreated curve. The full three-block spectral derivative yields a possibly singular joint Gaussian law; positive coordinate variances suffice for the simultaneous band and a positive grid-RMST variance suffices for scalar studentization. Weak-gap and selected-rank inference remains open.

project_justification.niche: With \(N_0,T_0,J,r\) fixed and \(K\to\infty\), covariate-standardized cell curves form a finite-dimensional semiparametric first stage and the counterfactual is a smooth spectral functional on a separated-rank neighborhood. project_justification.fill: The project proves the conditional-learner AIPCW cell expansion, a finite-stratum clipped-hazard attainability certificate, the joint transported Gaussian law with possibly singular covariance, a Gaussian-multiplier band under positive coordinate variances, and a studentized grid-RMST interval under positive variance in that scalar direction. sampling_model.treatment: The target switches treatment after the pre period while donor units remain under control. Exact post-transport equates the observed-law functional \(yM_r^+B\) with the target's untreated post-period survival row; target-pre row membership is not needed by the joint limit theorem.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Fixed-fold cross-fitting estimates conditional event and censor survival. The positive theorem is conditional on \(a_K\to0\), \(b_K\to0\), \(a_Kb_K=o(K^{-1/2})\), origin normalization, bounded variation of \(R_{cf}\), and \(\max_{c,f,\ell}\|V_{cf\ell}(X)\|_{L_2(P_c)}=O_P(a_K)\). The last two are substantive learner restrictions, not consequences of generic machine-learning consistency. On a fixed finite support for covariates and event times, clipped empirical conditional hazard ratios and their finite product integral attain \(a_K=K^{-1/2}\); any consistent censor learner with \(b_K=o(1)\) then satisfies the product rate. This finite-stratum certificate is not asserted for generic learners or for the TCL application.

prose_updates.related_work: Han and Shah (2025, Theorems 1--2 and Appendix E) supply the fixed-grid latent-factor survival panel, unit and time spans, PCR transport, and the 925-patient, 10-country TCL application. They assume event-time/censoring conditional independence given treatment and covariates, but use marginal cellwise Kaplan--Meier inputs and do not derive a covariate-adjusted transported influence law. Proposition~\ref{prop:han-shah-fixed-grid-embedding} gives their algebraic span bridge, while the joint limit itself needs exact post-transport but not target-pre row membership. Westling, Luedtke, Gilbert, and Carone (2024, published Theorem 3 (arXiv Theorem 4) and Sections 5.2--5.3) supply direct-curve cross-fitted augmented survival inference. The relative-survival variation restriction here is an additional primitive sufficient condition not imposed by Westling et al., who instead assume the exact Stieltjes-remainder rate. Proposition~\ref{prop:finite-stratum-hazard-certificate} proves that restriction for a fixed finite-stratum clipped empirical hazard learner, not for generic learners. Agarwal, Shah, and Shen (2025, Theorem 2 and Corollary 2) study minimum-norm PCR and row-space prediction without censoring-aware asymptotics. Golub and Pereyra (1973, equation (4.12)) provide the constant-rank pseudoinverse differential. Curth, Poon, Nori, and Gonz\'alez (2024, Sections 3--4) analyze survival synthetic-control bias but not this three-block PCR pseudo-limit. Fan and Liao (2022) study growing-panel factor models, and Choi, Kwon, and Liao (2026) study robustness to rank misspecification. These are neighboring problems; weak-gap and selected-rank inference for the unregularized fixed-donor target remains an acknowledged open frontier of this note.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The positive theory is fixed-dimensional and conditional on an event learner whose relative-survival path has the stated bounded variation and \(L_2\) variation rate. Ordinary supremum or \(L_2\) consistency does not imply that property. The finite-stratum hazard certificate establishes attainability only for fixed covariate and event-time supports with uniformly positive at-risk probabilities, event hazards bounded away from one, and proportional training samples; it does not verify the restriction for generic learners or for the TCL data. The joint Gaussian covariance may be singular, but the band excludes zero counterfactual coordinate variances and the grid-RMST interval excludes zero variance in its scalar direction. The theory does not cover growing grids or panels, a shrinking singular gap, selected rank, approximate post-transport, or continuous-time RMST.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The joint cell expansion is a conditional-learner theorem under within-cell i.i.d. sampling, cross-cell independence for stacking, conditional independent censoring, censor positivity, fixed-fold nuisance consistency and product rate, origin normalization, and explicit bounded-variation and relative-variation restrictions. A concrete clipped empirical hazard learner discharges the event-side restrictions with root-\(K\) rate only on the stated fixed finite-stratum submodel; this does not establish generic learner attainability or verify the 925-patient TCL application. The spectral limit additionally requires fixed panel dimensions, exact rank, a fixed singular gap, and exact post-transport, which is its sole causal-identification equality; target-pre row membership remains only in the Han--Shah embedding and converse uses. The joint covariance may be singular. The simultaneous band requires positive counterfactual marginal variances, and the studentized grid-RMST interval separately requires positive variance of \(q^\top(\Phi_1-\Phi_\theta)\). Applying either conclusion to TCL requires independent verification of all sampling, learner, transport, and relevant variance conditions. Nothing here covers growing dimensions, weak gaps, selected rank, approximate transport, or continuous-time RMST. Weak-gap inference remains the acknowledged follow-on question because its frontier also depends on weak loadings and a uniform triangular experiment, not only on \(\sigma_r(M_K)\).

proofs.proof_tex:
We first establish the probability limit and the continuity assertion.  For a cell \(c\) and a time \(u\) in a fixed finite support, define the empirical event submass and empirical risk probability by
\[
 \widehat d_{cK}(u)=\frac1K\sum_{i=1}^K
       \mathbf 1\{U_{ci}=u,\Delta_{ci}=1\},\qquad
 \widehat R_{cK}(u)=\frac1K\sum_{i=1}^K
       \mathbf 1\{U_{ci}\ge u\},
\]
and let \(d_c(u)\) and \(R_c(u)\) denote their expectations under \(P_c\).  By \(\mathrm{ass{:}cell\mbox{-}iid}\), each summand is Bernoulli and hence
\[
 \operatorname{Var}\{\widehat d_{cK}(u)\}\le \frac{1}{4K},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}\{\widehat R_{cK}(u)\}\le \frac{1}{4K}.
\]
Consequently, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), Markov's inequality applied to the squared centered mean gives
\[
 P_c\!\left(\left|\widehat d_{cK}(u)-d_c(u)\right|>\varepsilon\right)
 \le \frac{1}{4K\varepsilon^2},\qquad
 P_c\!\left(\left|\widehat R_{cK}(u)-R_c(u)\right|>\varepsilon\right)
 \le \frac{1}{4K\varepsilon^2}.
\]
The fixed-panel condition \(\mathrm{ass{:}fixed\mbox{-}panel}\) makes the total number of cells and retained coordinates finite.  A finite union bound therefore yields joint convergence of all these empirical submasses and risk probabilities.  Wherever \(R_c(u)>0\), division is continuous, and the empirical Kaplan--Meier product consequently satisfies
\[
 \widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{cK}(t_{c\ell})
 =\prod_{u\le t_{c\ell}}
   \left\{1-\frac{\widehat d_{cK}(u)}{\widehat R_{cK}(u)}\right\}
 \xrightarrow{p}
 \prod_{u\le t_{c\ell}}
   \left\{1-\frac{d_c(u)}{R_c(u)}\right\}
 =\widetilde S_c(t_{c\ell}).
\]
This proves the cellwise probability-limit assertion on the finite discrete submodel with positive risk denominators.  In the general product-integral formulation of \(\mathrm{def{:}km\mbox{-}pcr\mbox{-}bias\mbox{-}map}\), \(\widetilde S_c\) is the corresponding marginal Kaplan--Meier probability limit; the remaining argument only uses convergence at the fixed retained coordinates.  Extracting blocks is linear, so
\[
 (\widehat y^{\mathrm{KM}},\widehat M^{\mathrm{KM}},
   \widehat B^{\mathrm{KM}})
 \xrightarrow{p}(\widetilde y,\widetilde M,\widetilde B).
\]

We next verify the required spectral continuity.  Let \(A_n\to A\) in operator norm and suppose
\[
 \sigma_r(A)>\sigma_{r+1}(A),
\]
where a missing singular value is interpreted as zero.  The variational characterization of singular values and the triangle inequality give
\[
 |\sigma_k(A_n)-\sigma_k(A)|\le \|A_n-A\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\]
for every \(k\).  Let \(\Pi_n\) be the orthogonal projector onto the leading \(r\) right singular subspace of \(A_n\).  The set of rank-\(r\) orthogonal projectors is compact.  Every convergent subsequence of \((\Pi_n)\) has a limit maximizing
\[
 Q\longmapsto \operatorname{tr}(Q A^\top A)
\]
over rank-\(r\) orthogonal projectors, because \(\Pi_n\) maximizes the analogous criterion with \(A_n^\top A_n\).  The strict singular gap makes this maximizer unique: it is the projector \(\Pi\) onto the leading \(r\) right singular subspace of \(A\).  Thus every convergent subsequence has limit \(\Pi\), and compactness implies \(\Pi_n\to\Pi\).  It follows that
\[
 (A_n)_r=A_n\Pi_n\longrightarrow A\Pi=A_r.
\]
Moreover, \(\sigma_r(A)>0\), so for all sufficiently large \(n\) the matrix
\[
 (A_n)_r^\top(A_n)_r+I-\Pi_n
\]
is invertible.  A singular-value decomposition verifies
\[
 (A_n)_r^+
 =\left\{(A_n)_r^\top(A_n)_r+I-\Pi_n\right\}^{-1}(A_n)_r^\top.
\]
Matrix inversion is continuous at an invertible matrix, and hence
\[
 (A_n)_r^+\longrightarrow A_r^+.
\]
Applying this result at \(A=\widetilde M\), whose separated rank supplies the required strict gap and positive \(r\)-th singular value, and then applying continuity of matrix multiplication proves
\[
 \widehat y^{\mathrm{KM}}
       (\widehat M^{\mathrm{KM}})_r^+
       \widehat B^{\mathrm{KM}}
 \xrightarrow{p}
 \widetilde y(\widetilde M)_r^+\widetilde B.
\]

Now parameterize the finite discrete submodel by its finitely many cell-atom probabilities.  Each true survival coordinate is a finite sum of event atom probabilities.  Each marginal Kaplan--Meier coordinate is a finite product of ratios of affine functions of the atom probabilities.  It is therefore continuous wherever every risk denominator is positive.  The preceding spectral argument shows that \(M\mapsto M_r^+\) and \(\widetilde M\mapsto(\widetilde M)_r^+\) are continuous wherever their rank-\(r\) singular gaps are positive.  Thus, by \(\mathrm{def{:}km\mbox{-}pcr\mbox{-}bias\mbox{-}map}\), the discrepancy map
\[
 p\longmapsto
 \beta_{\mathrm{KM}}(p)
 =\widetilde y(p)(\widetilde M(p))_r^+\widetilde B(p)
  -y(p)(M(p))_r^+B(p)
\]
is continuous on that domain.  Let \(\mathcal S\) denote the finite-support submodel satisfying \(\mathrm{ass{:}conditional\mbox{-}censoring}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}censor\mbox{-}positivity}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}exact\mbox{-}rank}\), and \(\mathrm{ass{:}post\mbox{-}transport}\), and define
\[
 \mathcal U=
 \left\{p\in\mathcal S:
   \begin{array}{l}
   \text{all required risks are positive, the true and naive rank-\(r\)}\\[-2pt]
   \text{singular gaps are positive, and }\|\beta_{\mathrm{KM}}(p)\|_2>0
   \end{array}
 \right\}.
\]
Positivity of finitely many risk denominators, strict singular gaps, and the strict inequality \(\|\beta_{\mathrm{KM}}(p)\|_2>0\) are open conditions.  Hence \(\mathcal U\) is relatively open in \(\mathcal S\).  It is an open subclass on which the well-defined unadjusted PCR probability limit differs from the transported causal curve \(\theta=yM_r^+B\).  The equality of the latter functional with the untreated causal curve is supplied by \(\mathrm{ass{:}post\mbox{-}transport}\); it is not part of the definition of the naive functional.

It remains to verify that the witness in \(\mathrm{def{:}rational\mbox{-}witness}\) belongs to \(\mathcal U\).  Its six displayed true survival pairs, including the repeated factual-post pair, are
\[
 (a,b)\in
 \left\{(7/10,9/20),(4/5,3/5),(3/5,3/10),
 (7/10,2/5),(1/2,1/5),(7/10,2/5)\right\}.
\]
For \(\epsilon_x=2x-1\), the three conditional event atom masses in that definition obey, uniformly over this list and \(x\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 1-a-\frac{\epsilon_x}{20}\ge\frac3{20},\qquad
 a-b+\frac{\epsilon_x}{40}\ge\frac7{40},\qquad
 b+\frac{\epsilon_x}{40}\ge\frac7{40}.
\]
They sum to one.  The three censor atom masses are, for \(x=0\),
\[
 (1-\gamma_{10},\gamma_{10}-\gamma_{20},\gamma_{20})
 =(1/5,3/10,1/2),
\]
and, for \(x=1\),
\[
 (1-\gamma_{11},\gamma_{11}-\gamma_{21},\gamma_{21})
 =(2/5,1/5,2/5).
\]
Thus every displayed atom mass is strictly positive.  Conditional independent censoring holds because the construction draws \(T_{ci}\) and \(C_{ci}\) independently given \(X_{ci}\), verifying \(\mathrm{ass{:}conditional\mbox{-}censoring}\).  Moreover,
\[
 P_c(T_{ci}>t_{c1}\mid X_{ci}=x)=a+\frac{\epsilon_x}{20},
 \qquad
 P_c(T_{ci}>t_{c2}\mid X_{ci}=x)=b+\frac{\epsilon_x}{40}.
\]
Because \(P_c(X_{ci}=0)=P_c(X_{ci}=1)=1/2\), averaging over \(X_{ci}\) gives the advertised marginal event-survival pair \((a,b)\).  Finally, for every \(0\le t\le t_{c2}\),
\[
 G_c(t\mid x)=P_c(C_{ci}\ge t\mid X_{ci}=x)
 \ge P_c(C_{ci}=\infty\mid X_{ci}=x)
 =\gamma_{2x}\ge\frac25,
\]
which verifies \(\mathrm{ass{:}censor\mbox{-}positivity}\) with \(g=2/5\) on the required horizon.

We next calculate the marginal Kaplan--Meier functional under the event-wins-ties convention \(\Delta_{ci}=\mathbf 1\{T_{ci}\le C_{ci}\}\).  At the first time,
\[
 R_c(t_{c1})=P_c(U_{ci}\ge t_{c1})=1,
 \qquad
 d_c(t_{c1})=P_c(U_{ci}=t_{c1},\Delta_{ci}=1)=1-a.
\]
At the second time, conditional independence and the two covariate strata give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 R_c(t_{c2})
 &=\frac12\left\{(a-1/20)\frac45+(a+1/20)\frac35\right\}\\
 &=\frac{140a-1}{200},
 \end{aligned}
\]
and
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 d_c(t_{c2})
 &=\frac12\left\{(a-b-1/40)\frac45
                   +(a-b+1/40)\frac35\right\}\\
 &=\frac{280(a-b)-1}{400}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The smallest displayed value of \(a\) is \(1/2\), so
\[
 R_c(t_{c2})\ge\frac{140(1/2)-1}{200}=\frac{69}{200}>0.
\]
The first Kaplan--Meier factor is \(1-(1-a)=a\), and the second gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \widetilde S_c(t_{c2})
 &=a\left\{1-
   \frac{[280(a-b)-1]/400}{(140a-1)/200}\right\}\\
 &=a\left\{1-\frac{280(a-b)-1}{280a-2}\right\}
 =\frac{a(280b-1)}{280a-2}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Therefore the marginal Kaplan--Meier pair is exactly
\[
 \left(a,\frac{a(280b-1)}{280a-2}\right).
\]
Substitution of the six pairs gives
\[
 \widetilde y=(7/10,175/388),\qquad
 \widetilde M=
 \begin{pmatrix}4/5&334/555\\3/5&3/10\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 \widetilde B=
 \begin{pmatrix}7/10&777/1940\\1/2&55/276\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The factual-post pair is the repeated pair \((7/10,2/5)\), so its naive limit is \((7/10,777/1940)\), and it is not an argument of the counterfactual map in \(\mathrm{def{:}km\mbox{-}pcr\mbox{-}bias\mbox{-}map}\).

For the true donor-pre matrix,
\[
 \det(M)=\frac45\frac3{10}-\frac35\frac35=-\frac3{25}\ne0.
\]
Thus \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=r=2\), verifying \(\mathrm{ass{:}exact\mbox{-}rank}\); its rank gap is positive.  Its row space is all of \(\mathbb R^2\), so \(\mathrm{ass{:}target\mbox{-}pre\mbox{-}span}\) also holds for the witness.  Direct inversion gives
\[
 yM^{-1}=(1/2,1/2),\qquad
 yM^{-1}B=(1/2,1/2)
 \begin{pmatrix}7/10&2/5\\1/2&1/5\end{pmatrix}
 =(3/5,3/10).
\]
The witness assigns its latent untreated target-post row to this vector, so \(\mathrm{ass{:}post\mbox{-}transport}\) holds and \(\theta=(3/5,3/10)\).  For the naive donor-pre matrix,
\[
 \det(\widetilde M)
 =\frac45\frac3{10}-\frac35\frac{334}{555}
 =-\frac{112}{925}\ne0.
\]
Hence the naive rank-two gap is positive and \((\widetilde M)_2^+=\widetilde M^{-1}\).  Exact elimination yields
\[
 \widetilde y\widetilde M^{-1}
 =\left(\frac{777}{1552},\frac{581}{1164}\right).
\]
Multiplying by \(\widetilde B\) coordinate by coordinate gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \widetilde y\widetilde M^{-1}\widetilde B
 &=\left(
 \frac{777}{1552}\frac7{10}+\frac{581}{1164}\frac12,
 \frac{777}{1552}\frac{777}{1940}
       +\frac{581}{1164}\frac{55}{276}
 \right)\\
 &=\left(\frac{27937}{46560},
          \frac{186964603}{623252160}\right)\\
 &=\left(\frac35+\frac1{46560},
          \frac3{10}-\frac{2209}{124650432}\right).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, by \(\mathrm{def{:}km\mbox{-}pcr\mbox{-}bias\mbox{-}map}\),
\[
 \beta_{\mathrm{KM}}(P^\star)
 =\left(\frac1{46560},-\frac{2209}{124650432}\right)\ne(0,0).
\]
Thus \(P^\star\in\mathcal U\).  Continuity supplies a relative neighborhood of \(P^\star\) inside the stated conditional-censoring, positivity, exact-rank, exact-transport submodel on which this nonzero discrepancy persists.  Since the unadjusted estimator converges there to \(\theta+\beta_{\mathrm{KM}}\), rather than to the causal curve \(\theta\), the bias is fixed and does not vanish as \(K\to\infty\).  This proves every assertion.

The asserted bridge is deterministic matrix algebra on the fixed grids.  From the displayed target-row factorization and the unit-factor-span condition,
\[
y=v_n^\top U_0=w^\top VU_0=w^\top M.
\]
Thus \(y\) is a linear combination of the rows of \(M\), so \(y\in\operatorname{row}(M)\).

By Assumption~\ref{ass:exact-rank}, \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=r\).  Hence the rank-\(r\) truncation is \(M_r=M\), and therefore \(M_r^+=M^+\).  The defining Moore--Penrose identity \(MM^+M=M\), together with \(y=w^\top M\), gives
\[
yM^+M=w^\top MM^+M=w^\top M=y.
\]
The post/pre time-factor-span condition yields
\[
B=VU_1=VU_0A=MA.
\]
Consequently,
\[
yM_r^+B
=yM^+MA
=yA
=v_n^\top U_0A
=v_n^\top U_1.
\]
The last expression is the latent untreated target-post row under the factor representation in the proposition.  Thus the observed-law functional \(yM_r^+B\) equals that latent causal target because of the stated factor and span restrictions; the equality is not definitional.

It remains to verify the claimed inclusion of the rational witness.  By Definition~\ref{def:rational-witness},
\[
M=
\begin{pmatrix}
4/5&3/5\\
3/5&3/10
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
y=(7/10,9/20),
\qquad
B=
\begin{pmatrix}
7/10&2/5\\
1/2&1/5
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Its determinant is
\[
\det(M)=\frac45\frac3{10}-\frac35\frac35
=\frac6{25}-\frac9{25}
=-\frac3{25}\ne0.
\]
Thus \(M\) has rank two, which equals \(r\) in the witness, and \(M_r^+=M^{-1}\).  Moreover,
\[
\left(\frac12,\frac12\right)M
=\left(\frac12\left(\frac45+\frac35\right),
        \frac12\left(\frac35+\frac3{10}\right)\right)
=\left(\frac7{10},\frac9{20}\right)
=y.
\]
Since \(M\) is invertible, right multiplication by \(M^{-1}\) gives
\[
yM^{-1}=\left(\frac12,\frac12\right).
\]
Set \(d=2\), \(V=I_2\), \(U_0=M\), \(U_1=B\), \(A=M^{-1}B\), and \(v_n^\top=yM^{-1}\).  Then, equation by equation,
\[
VU_0=M,
\qquad
v_n^\top U_0=yM^{-1}M=y,
\qquad
VU_1=B,
\qquad
U_0A=MM^{-1}B=B=U_1.
\]
Taking \(w=v_n\) gives \(v_n^\top=w^\top V\), so the unit-factor-span condition also holds.  Finally,
\[
\theta=yM_r^+B
=yM^{-1}B
=\left(\frac12,\frac12\right)
\begin{pmatrix}
7/10&2/5\\
1/2&1/5
\end{pmatrix}
=\left(\frac35,\frac3{10}\right).
\]
This proves both the fixed-grid embedding and the stated value for \(P^\star\).  No censoring, positivity, boundary, or limiting condition is used in this algebraic proposition.
